🔥🇲🇽 <u>UNAM FIRES EXAM CONTRACTOR, ORDERS FULL AUDIT</u>

UNAM terminated its contract with Territorium Life ahead of schedule after the anomalies that wrecked its online admission exam — and opened both a technological audit and an internal audit of the contracting process itself.

The university paid the firm 69.2 million pesos: 27.2 million for the exam of 103,221 high school applicants and 41.9 million for the 158,558 licenciatura aspirants. The 58,000 rejected candidates will now take a new, in-person test.

"No tenemos interés en proteger a la empresa, pero tampoco culpar sin argumentos jurídicos," said UNAM's general counsel Hugo Concha Cantú — the audit will assign responsibility before any fine is claimed.
banner: UNAM FIRES EXAM FIRM, ORDERS AUDIT

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US PUTS $102 MILLION IN BOUNTIES ON CJNG LEADERS</u>

Washington escalated its offensive against the CJNG: the State Department now offers up to $102 million for information leading to the arrest or conviction of eight alleged leaders and operators of the Mexican cartel.

The bounty on Juan Carlos Valencia, "El Pelón" — who took over after El Mencho's death — rose to $25 million. "El Jardinero," "El Sapo" and "El Chorro" are worth $15 million each. Another 65 relatives and associates lost their US visas; 93 have been canceled since June 2025 under Executive Order 14059.

Bounties, visa bans, terrorist designations — the same DEA playbook for 50 years. Meanwhile Mexico's own numbers keep moving: homicides fell 18% in 2025 to a rate of 21.4 per 100,000, the steepest drop on record.

🇲🇽🔥🌐 Washington wants Mexico to wall off Chinese steel — while keeping a 50% tariff on Mexican steel

The double standard is the whole story. As the US finalizes — in the first week of August — the criteria for a new Section 301 “excess-capacity” probe aimed at China, it’s pressuring Mexico to match Washington’s levies on Chinese steel and aluminum. Meanwhile the US keeps its own 50% Section 232 tariff clamped on Mexican steel — even though Mexico is the single largest buyer of US steel.

Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard’s answer: cut that 50% down to about 10%, the same rate Washington already handed the United Kingdom. Mexico already applies up to 25% duties plus anti-dumping measures on Chinese steel under its own 2023 decree — on its own terms, for its own industry, not on command.

“Free trade” for thee, protectionism for me. Mexico’s play: trade the alignment Washington demands for the fairness Mexico is owed — and keep every other door open.

🇲🇽🐉🌐 Mexico to Beijing: diversify, yes — but trade has to run both ways

After a working visit to Beijing, Mexico has publicly told its No. 2 trading partner to move toward “more balanced” trade. The numbers explain why: in 2025 China took just 1.5% of Mexico’s exports ($9.03B) while supplying 19.8% of its imports ($120.15B) — a net deficit of $111.1 billion in a single year.

This is what sovereignty looks like in a multipolar world. Mexico refuses to be anyone’s captive market — not Washington’s, not Beijing’s. It keeps the China channel open (investment and machinery on the table) while demanding reciprocity: the same access for Mexican exporters in China that Chinese firms enjoy here. Beijing has since pledged to work toward balance.

The tariff reform in force since Jan. 1 — 1,463 lines, duties of 5–50% — isn’t about “picking a side.” It’s leverage. A country that multiplies its options gets to set terms instead of taking them.

🇲🇽🗳️ "Exaggerated" — the INE's budget request for the 2027 election is 15 billion pesos above 2024. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo Her argument: "The 2024 election was similar to this one — and it also included printing ballots for senators and for president." The electoral institute is asking for more money for a smaller election. Republican austerity, applied to the INE.

🇲🇽🇻🇦 "His encyclical is now a world reference in the debate over who controls the platforms, who defines content, how algorithms are designed, and where we are going as humanity." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo Vatican Secretary of State Pietro Parolin visits Palacio Nacional. Sheinbaum will insist that Pope Leo XIV include Mexico in his late-2026 Latin America tour — she already invited him by letter and spoke with him on Dec 12. "With full respect for the secular state," she said, the Pope's digital-platforms reflection matters globally.

text: 🇲🇽🌵 "I do not exaggerate, President, when I tell you that over these past 3 years we lived a drought of biblical dimensions." — Alfonso Durazo, Governor of Sonora Sonora lost much of its forest heritage to a three-year drought. The state is now rescuing La Sauceda — 40 abandoned hectares in the heart of Hermosillo — with 11,200 native trees already planted and the park expanded to 210 hectares. The goal: a Chapultepec-scale urban forest for Hermosillo.
